editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout, with the informal register kept ("Chceš-li použít dovednost AI pro Qiskit, postupuj…"); "skill" is consistently rendered "dovednost AI", and entry [5] ("stačí dovednost asistentovi předat a poté mu říct, kde ji má použít") matches the source exactly.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The optimization-level comparison, the seed caveat, the dynamical-decoupling claims and the Hellinger fidelity explanation (higher is better, 1 is perfect) all match the English, and no sentence would mislead a learner. There are some small fixes. Entry [17] has a case error, "do obvod transpilovaného", which should be "do obvodu". Entries [0] and [5] are stiff calques ("celým procesem vytváření", "vyvinut s použitím následujících požadavků"). "Ideal distribution" is rendered as "ideální distribuce" where Czech statistics normally says "rozdělení", and "Qubity se dekoherují" in [13] reads oddly as a reflexive verb.

The paragraph right below it (entry 24) and the link text in entry 27 ("dokumentaci Qiskit Functions") keep the name "Qiskit Functions" as-is, and so do the sibling headings "Qiskit Serverless" and "IBM Quantum Platform". The English word order "Qiskit funkce" is also unidiomatic in Czech; entry 24 uses the natural order in "Katalog funkcí Qiskit". The heading doesn't mislead anyone, but it should read "Qiskit Functions" to match the rest of the page.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and the key points come through intact: the role requirements in [5] and the claim in [4] that context-based restrictions protect even when credentials are compromised. One small problem: the page description [0] renders "define and enforce restrictions on resources" as "definování a vynucování přístupu ke zdrojům" ("defining and enforcing access"). Two other things a native editor would likely change: the IBM Cloud role names are translated ("roli Prohlížeče", "Administrátora", "Editora") where the UI shows Viewer/Editor/Administrator, and "tutorial" in [7] becomes "výukový kurz" when it points to a single page.

editor_note: Entry [1], "Integrace externích kvantových zdrojů s Qiskitem", is faithful and reads naturally. It uses the usual Czech noun-style title for the English imperative, and it matches the heading in [2] word for word.

The meaning holds throughout. The AnalysisPass/TransformationPass read/write rules, the "before/after" cancellation of the twirls and the coherent-to-stochastic claim all match the English. The main issue is that "pass" has two renderings: entry [6] uses the anglicism "pass/passy/passu", while every later entry uses "průchod". "Noisy channels" in [17] becomes "hlučnými kanály", which means acoustically loud, even though [6] correctly says "zašuměných". In [20], "subcircuit" is narrowed to "podgrafem" instead of "podobvodem", and "apply_operation_front by ho umístil" has the wrong gender for "metoda"/"operace".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The ZNE/PEA/PEC caveats (no guarantee of an unbiased result, the PEC overhead scaling, the max_overhead precision note) all carry over correctly, so a learner would not be misled. Several word choices still need a native editor. [10] renders 'identity operation' as 'identické operaci' ('identical operation') instead of 'operaci identity'. [24] uses 'k vyčerpání' ('to exhaust') for 'to draw' instead of 'k vybrání'. [31] renders statistical 'bias' as 'zaujatost', which means human prejudice; 'zkreslení' is the right word. [7] has the typo 'Tata stránka' and the calque 'vysvětlení na vysoké úrovni', [70] misspells 'režije', and [39] strengthens 'often' to 'obvykle'.

Entry 8 renders "We acknowledge the use of IBM Quantum services for this work" as "Potvrzujeme použití služeb IBM Quantum pro tuto práci". That copies the English wording too closely. "Potvrzujeme" means "we confirm", which does not fit the acknowledgments section of a paper, and "pro tuto práci" sounds stiff. A Czech paper would write "V této práci byly využity služby IBM Quantum" or "Děkujeme za možnost využití služeb IBM Quantum". The disclaimer sentence in entry 8 and all of entry 12 ("jeden z procesorů IBM Quantum Canary") are accurate and read naturally.

examples.suggested: V této práci byly využity služby IBM Quantum.
examples.why: Here "acknowledge" works as a thank-you in the acknowledgments section. "Potvrzujeme" means "we confirm", so it copies the English word but misses its function. "pro tuto práci" is also stiff. A Czech author would not write this in a paper's acknowledgments.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The angle range, the parameter caveat, the note about copied error rates, the list of unsupported mitigation techniques and the fake-backend behaviour all match the English. A native editor would still fix three things. First, "až o faktor dvou" in [9] is a calque of "by up to a factor of two". Second, "fractional" is rendered "zlomkový" but "non-fractional" becomes "nefrakční" in [12] and [13], mixing two word roots. Third, "možnostmi primitive" in [33] is an awkward half-translation.

editor_note: In the Singularity Machine Learning row, the ML term "learners" (the base models in an ensemble) is translated twice as "učitelé", which means "teachers". That gives the opposite role and suggests teacher-student distillation, a different ML concept, so a reader would get a false idea of what the quantum-optimized voting selects. Smaller problems: "shots" is calqued as "snímků" (photographs). "end-to-end" is rendered as the odd "na celý řetězec". The section heading "Obvodové funkce" doesn't match "Circuit function(s)" used in the tables. "overhead" is left untranslated and not declined ("s nulovým overhead").

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (5, 6, 26) keep the English meaning: client-side pre- and post-processing, execution delegated to Executor, and the import statement as the only change are all intact. Nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix three small things. In entry 5, "jemnější kontrolu" calques "finer control", and in Czech "kontrola" suggests inspection, so "jemnější řízení" is better. In entry 26, the last bullet "Zobrazit API…" switches to an infinitive and breaks the informal imperative pattern of the other bullets. In the same entry, "lekci cost function" leaves the term in English where "nákladová funkce" is the usual Czech.

examples.suggested: …rychlejší zpětnou vazbu při ladění a jemnější řízení.

editor_note: Both rewritten descriptions keep the English meaning. Entry 12 ("Prozkoumej naši bezplatnou vzdělávací nabídku, jako jsou celé kurzy a výukové moduly") is accurate and natural. The problem is that entries 12 and 13 leave their visible card text in English: title="Learning", linkText="Visit IBM Quantum Learning", title="Learning paths" and linkText="Explore learning paths". Every other card on the page translates these fields ("Rychlý start", "Procházet tutoriály", "Zobrazit úvod"), so these two cards look unfinished next to them. Also, "promyšlené sekvence" in entry 13 is a stiff calque of "curated sequences". A Czech writer would say "pečlivě sestavené posloupnosti" or "řady".

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries misleads a learner. The meaning holds throughout, including the dropped-caveat check on [23] ("nemá vestavěné potlačování ani zmírňování chyb") and the version and fake-backend guidance in [25]. A native editor would still make three small changes. In [19], "úpravy ansatz" leaves the term undeclined, and Czech technical prose would write "úpravy ansatzu". In [28], "General-purpose" is rendered as "Víceúčelová", which means multi-purpose; "Univerzální" is the usual word. Also in [28], the column header keeps the English "Fake Backends", while the surrounding prose ([25], [29], [31]) says "falešné backendy".

editor_note: I found no meaning drift. The caveats come through intact: in [23], every option except shots is ignored on a local simulator; in [29], the Aer noise model is probably milder than real QPU noise; in [20]/[21], the unitary and superop methods do not support measurement. The issues are about wording and consistency. 'Fake backends' appears as 'falešných backendů' in [9] but stays in English in [10], [23] and [25], and 'shot' is rendered as 'výstřel' in [15] but left as 'shots' in [23]. There are also two stiff calques: [18] 'stabilizátorového stavu s hodností' for 'ranked-stabilizer state', and [19], which says 'reprezentaci' twice in one clause. The link label for the Transpile section in [37] also changes to 'Transpiler'.

examples.translation: bez ohledu na to, zda posunout rozsah možných středních hodnot nahoru nebo dolů nebo zvětšit rozptyl
examples.suggested: bez ohledu na to, zda posuneš rozsah možných středních hodnot nahoru či dolů nebo ho roztáhneš
examples.why: An infinitive after 'zda' is ungrammatical here. Also, 'rozptyl' suggests statistical variance, while the source means the width of the range.

examples.source: variational quantum eigensolver
examples.translation: variačního kvantového eigensolverú
examples.suggested: variačního kvantového eigensolveru
examples.why: Typo in the genitive ending: 'ú' should be 'u'.

examples.source: a single circuit-observable pair
examples.translation: jeden pár Circuit-observables
examples.suggested: jednu dvojici obvodu a observable
examples.why: This mixes English in a hyphenated compound, with a plural 'observables' that isn't in the source. It reads as a raw calque.

editor_note: The page is short, faithful and consistently uses the informal "ty" register (Podívej se, Nainstaluj, Přečti si). Two wordings need a fix. In [3], "přerušuje kompatibilitu" means "interrupts compatibility", which is a calque; the usual Czech is "narušuje kompatibilitu" or "není zpětně kompatibilní". In [6], "Breaking package changes" became "Zásadní změny balíčků" ("major changes"), which drops the idea that these changes break existing code. "Nekompatibilní změny" keeps that meaning. Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: but it does break compatibility with all previous versions of Qiskit
examples.translation: ale přerušuje kompatibilitu se všemi předchozími verzemi Qiskit
examples.suggested: ale narušuje kompatibilitu se všemi předchozími verzemi Qiskitu
examples.why: 'Přerušovat' means to interrupt or pause, so it is a calque of 'break'. Czech technical writing says 'narušit/rozbít kompatibilitu' or 'není zpětně kompatibilní'.

examples.source: Breaking package changes of Qiskit v1.0
examples.translation: Zásadní změny balíčků v Qiskit v1.0
examples.suggested: Nekompatibilní změny balíčků v Qiskit v1.0
examples.why: 'Breaking changes' means changes that break existing code. 'Zásadní' only means 'major', so the warning about incompatibility is weakened.

editor_note: Entry 3 translates "error mitigation" as "potlačení chyb", which means error suppression. IBM treats suppression and mitigation as two separate techniques, and this same page keeps them apart: entry 5 has "potlačení a zmírnění chyb" and entry 7 has "zmírnění chyb". A learner would therefore take the example to mean error suppression, not mitigation, so entry 3 should use "zmírnění chyb". A smaller point in entry 9: "lekci cost function" leaves the lesson name in English inside Czech grammar, and "lekci o nákladové funkci" reads better.

examples.source: They provide a more sophisticated implementation (for example, by including error mitigation)
examples.translation: Poskytují sofistikovanější implementaci (například s potlačením chyb)
examples.suggested: Poskytují sofistikovanější implementaci (například se zmírněním chyb)
examples.why: 'potlačení chyb' means error suppression, a separate IBM technique. Entries 5 and 7 on this page use 'zmírnění chyb' for mitigation, so entry 3 names the wrong technique.

examples.source: working through the [Cost function lesson]
examples.translation: v [lekci cost function]
examples.suggested: v [lekci o nákladové funkci]
examples.why: An untranslated English noun phrase in a Czech case construction reads awkwardly. The Czech term is more natural.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: the level-0 to level-3 table, the ECR counts (six, six, six, three, then two with approximation_degree) and the fidelity passage all match the English. The problems are small. Lowercase "qubit" is left uninflected where Czech needs "qubitů" ("čísla qubit", "127 qubit", "nejlepších qubit"). [25] has a grammar error, "kterých je dva", which should be "kterých jsou dva". The tutorial title "Build repetition codes" is rendered as "opakujících se kódů" when the standard term is "opakovací kódy". In [7] the level-1 hedge "to try to select" was dropped, so VF2LayoutPostLayout now sounds like it always finds the best qubits.

examples.source: down to a circuit that only contains the active qubits, of which there are two
examples.translation: na obvod obsahující pouze aktivní qubit, kterých je dva
examples.suggested: na obvod obsahující pouze aktivní qubity, kterých jsou dva
examples.why: Grammar error: 'dva' takes the plural verb 'jsou', and 'qubit' needs to be inflected.

examples.source: Try the [Build repetition codes] tutorial.
examples.translation: Vyzkoušej tutoriál [Sestavení opakujících se kódů]
examples.suggested: Vyzkoušej tutoriál [Sestavení opakovacích kódů]
examples.why: The established Czech QEC term is 'opakovací kód'. 'Opakující se kódy' means 'codes that recur'.

examples.source: then it uses `VF2LayoutPostLayout` to try to select the best qubits in the graph
examples.translation: poté se použije `VF2LayoutPostLayout` k výběru nejlepších qubit v grafu
examples.suggested: poté se použije `VF2LayoutPostLayout`, který se pokusí vybrat nejlepší qubity v grafu
examples.why: The 'try' hedge was dropped, which makes the claim stronger than the English. The genitive plural 'qubitů' is also missing.

examples.source: selects the same physical qubit numbers as virtual
examples.translation: jako fyzické vybrána stejná čísla qubit jako virtuální
examples.suggested: vybere pro fyzické qubity stejná čísla jako pro virtuální
examples.why: Uninflected 'qubit' plus calqued word order make this read stiffly.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The exam facts all carry over correctly: 20 questions, at least 16 to pass, a temporary lock after two failed attempts, and the Credly data-sharing notice. There are a few small polish problems. The course title stays in English with English quotes ("Basics of Quantum Information") in [5], but [1] and [7] use the Czech "Základy kvantové informace". Gender forms are mixed: [5] has the inclusive "pomohl/a", while [8] and [9] use only the masculine "použil" and "připraven". "k nárokování odznaku" in [12] is a calque of "claiming the badge".

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "Basics of Quantum Information" course by IBM!
examples.translation: Gratulujeme k dokončení kurzu "Basics of Quantum Information" od IBM!
examples.suggested: Gratulujeme k dokončení kurzu „Základy kvantové informace“ od IBM!
examples.why: The course title here doesn't match the Czech title used in [1] and [7], and the quotes are English ("…") instead of Czech („…“).

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: s pokyny k nárokování odznaku
examples.suggested: s pokyny, jak si odznak převzít
examples.why: "Nárokování" is a calque of "claiming". A native writer would say "převzít" or "vyzvednout".

examples.source: the email you used to register with IBM Training
examples.translation: na e-mail, který jsi použil při registraci
examples.suggested: na e-mail, který jsi použil/a při registraci (or: na e-mail zadaný při registraci)
examples.why: This is only masculine, while [5] uses the inclusive "pomohl/a". The same inconsistency appears in [9] ("připraven").

editor_note: Faithful, natural Czech with correct terms: inner products are rendered "skalární součiny", no-cloning as "teorém o nemožnosti klonování" and standard basis measurements as "měření ve standardní bázi", and the informal "ty" register holds ("provede tě", "Stáhni si slajdy").

The meaning is faithful throughout, and the core terms are correct: stabilizátorový formalismus/kódy, pozorovatelné veličiny, tenzorové součiny Pauliho matic. Two sentences read as calques. In [3], "To nás informuje a povede k obecné diskuzi" copies "inform and lead into" word for word, which is unidiomatic in Czech. In [2], "se zdají být dobře vhodné" is stiff; "se zdají být vhodné" or "dobře se hodí" reads more naturally.

examples.source: This will both inform and lead into a general discussion of stabilizer codes
examples.translation: To nás informuje a povede k obecné diskuzi o stabilizátorových kódech
examples.suggested: To nám poslouží jako východisko a přirozeně nás dovede k obecné diskuzi o stabilizátorových kódech
examples.why: 'Informuje' is a literal calque of 'inform' and does not work idiomatically in Czech here.

examples.source: codes that seem likely to be well-suited to real-world quantum devices
examples.translation: kódů, které se zdají být dobře vhodné pro reálná kvantová zařízení
examples.suggested: kódů, které se pravděpodobně dobře hodí pro reálná kvantová zařízení
examples.why: 'dobře vhodné' is a stiff calque of 'well-suited', and it also drops the 'likely' hedge.

editor_note: The meaning matches the English throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The lower-bound claim, the O(√N) worst case and "may not lead … any time soon" (rendered "nemusí v blízké době vést") all come through correctly. The problems are English sentence structure carried into Czech. Entry [5] opens with "Nakonec, technika … může být zobecněna": the comma after the opener and the passive voice both copy the English. Entry [6] has "Takže, ačkoli…" and "je reprezentativní pro", and entry [2] has "přijít s dotazovacím algoritmem", a word-for-word copy of "come up with". A native technical writer would reword all of these.

examples.source: Finally, the technique used in Grover's algorithm, where two reflections are composed and iterated to rotate a quantum state vector, can be generalized.
examples.translation: Nakonec, technika použitá v Groverově algoritmu, kde se dvě reflexe skládají a iterují za účelem rotace vektoru kvantového stavu, může být zobecněna.
examples.suggested: Techniku z Groverova algoritmu, v níž se skládáním a opakováním dvou reflexí otáčí stavový vektor, lze navíc zobecnit.
examples.why: The comma after 'Nakonec', the passive 'může být zobecněna' and the phrase 'za účelem rotace' all copy English structure. Czech prefers 'lze zobecnit' with an active verb.

examples.source: So, although Grover's algorithm may not lead to a practical quantum advantage ... it is representative of a more general technique
examples.translation: Takže, ačkoli Groverův algoritmus ... je reprezentativní pro obecnější techniku
examples.suggested: Ačkoli tedy Groverův algoritmus ... je představitelem obecnější techniky
examples.why: 'Takže,' with a comma and 'je reprezentativní pro' are calques. 'tedy' placed inside the clause and 'je představitelem' read more naturally.

examples.source: it's not possible to come up with a query algorithm
examples.translation: není možné přijít s dotazovacím algoritmem
examples.suggested: nelze sestrojit dotazovací algoritmus
examples.why: 'přijít s' is a word-for-word copy of 'come up with' and sounds colloquial in mathematical prose.

editor_note: The rewritten entry [0], "Bezplatný kurz IBM o kvantové informaci a výpočtech", is faithful and natural, and "quantum" carries over both nouns just as it does in the English.

The meaning matches the English throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. Terms are right (dotazovací model výpočtu, orákulum, podprogramy, výpočetní náklady), and the informal "ty" register holds (tě provede, můžeš, Stáhni si). A few sentences read like calques of the English and a native editor would rewrite them. In [3], "se ukáže jako mnohem složitější otázka k zodpovězení" is stiff. In [4], "pro lekci následující po této" copies the English word order. In [6], "Důvod … není ten, že … ale spíše proto, že" mixes two sentence patterns, and "kriticky důležité" is copied word for word from "critically important".

examples.source: This turns out to be a much more difficult question to answer
examples.translation: To se ukáže jako mnohem složitější otázka k zodpovězení
examples.suggested: Ukazuje se, že na tuto otázku je mnohem těžší odpovědět
examples.why: "otázka k zodpovězení" is a calque of the English; the suggested wording is how Czech would say it.

examples.source: highly relevant to the lesson following this one
examples.translation: vysoce relevantní pro lekci následující po této
examples.suggested: velmi důležité pro následující lekci
examples.why: This copies the English word order; "pro následující lekci" is simpler and more natural.

examples.source: The reason this task is important is not because we hope ... but rather because it opens up
examples.translation: Důvod, proč je tato úloha důležitá, není ten, že bychom doufali ... ale spíše proto, že to otevírá
examples.suggested: Tato úloha není důležitá proto, že bychom doufali ..., ale proto, že otevírá
examples.why: "není ten, že" and "ale spíše proto, že" do not fit together in one sentence. "kriticky důležité" in the same entry is also a calque; "zásadně důležité" would be better.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and use the informal "ty" register ("Věnuj chvíli a pomoz nám", "Tvé osobní údaje", "si můžeš prohlédnout [zde]"); entry 12 keeps every caveat, including "IBM může sdílet … s dceřinými společnostmi IBM a třetími stranami po celém světě".

The three rewritten entries are faithful and use the informal "ty" register: [9] renders density matrices/channels/measurements as "maticemi hustoty"/"kanály"/"měření" and "in operational ways" as "z operačního hlediska"; [12] keeps the exam-then-Credly-notification order ("tě Credly upozorní, že jsi získal/a odznak"); [17] keeps the full data-sharing caveat (jméno, e-mailová adresa a získaný odznak).

Entry 109 renders the heading "Superdense coding" as "Superhusté kódování", which is the standard Czech term, and the anchor is intact. The body text in entries 110, 113 and 114 still leaves "superdense coding" in English, but that falls to the separate leak sweep and was not part of this delta.

The page is faithful and uses the informal "ty" throughout, but three slips need fixing. In [16], "personal information collected" became "sdílené osobní údaje" (the shared personal data), which reads oddly because the same sentence is about sharing it. It should be "shromážděné". In [9], "quantum information" is rendered in the plural as "kvantových informací", where Czech convention is the singular "kvantová informace" (Základy kvantové informace). In [0], "vysoce výkonné počítání" is stiff next to the usual "vysoce výkonné výpočty".

examples.source: IBM may share the personal information collected with IBM subsidiaries
examples.translation: IBM může sdílené osobní údaje předávat dceřiným společnostem IBM
examples.suggested: IBM může shromážděné osobní údaje sdílet s dceřinými společnostmi IBM
examples.why: 'collected' was rendered as 'sdílené' (shared), which changes which data is meant and sounds circular.

examples.source: Basics of quantum information
examples.translation: Základy kvantových informací
examples.suggested: Základy kvantové informace
examples.why: The field term in Czech is the singular 'kvantová informace'.

examples.source: quantum and high-performance computing
examples.translation: kvantové a vysoce výkonné počítání
examples.suggested: kvantové a vysoce výkonné výpočty
examples.why: 'výpočty' is the usual Czech rendering for HPC. 'počítání' sounds colloquial and stiff here.

editor_note: The translation is faithful: the pass threshold ("alespoň na 16" of 20), the two-attempt lockout and the Credly data-sharing terms all match the English, and the "ty" register holds throughout. Two small fixes are worth making. In the privacy notice [12], "IBM subsidiaries" became "pobočkami IBM" (branches), which is a legal term that should read "dceřinými společnostmi IBM". In the opening line [0], "20otázkovou zkoušku" is an awkward compound, and "zkoušku o 20 otázkách" reads more naturally.

examples.source: IBM may share the personal information collected with IBM subsidiaries and third parties globally.
examples.translation: IBM může sdílet shromážděné osobní údaje s pobočkami IBM a třetími stranami po celém světě.
examples.suggested: IBM může shromážděné osobní údaje sdílet s dceřinými společnostmi IBM a třetími stranami po celém světě.
examples.why: In a privacy notice, 'subsidiaries' means dceřiné společnosti (separate legal entities). 'Pobočky' means branches, which is a different legal concept.

examples.source: Take a 20-question exam on the IBM Training site
examples.translation: Slož 20otázkovou zkoušku na stránce IBM Training
examples.suggested: Slož zkoušku o 20 otázkách na stránce IBM Training
examples.why: The numeral compound '20otázková' is a stiff calque of '20-question'. A native writer would use a prepositional phrase.

editor_note: Entry 21 "Krok 4: Následné zpracování" is a faithful, natural Czech rendering of "Step 4: Post-processing", matching the parallel step headings (Krok 1–3); note only that entry 19, outside this delta, still says "post-processingu".

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 36 correctly keeps 0 as no optimization, 1 as the default, the 0/1/2/3 range in other contexts, and the reason for skip_transpilation (the circuit was already transpiled with the pass manager). Entry 37 is also accurate, but it switches to formal address ("Chcete-li se dozvědět více … přečtěte si"). The rest of the page, including entry 36 ("tvého obvodu", "najdeš"), uses informal "ty", so this is a register slip and should read "Chceš-li se dozvědět více …, přečti si".

examples.source: To learn about resilience level settings, refer to the [documentation]
examples.translation: Chcete-li se dozvědět více o nastavení úrovně odolnosti, přečtěte si [dokumentaci]
examples.suggested: Chceš-li se dozvědět více o nastavení úrovně odolnosti, přečti si [dokumentaci]
examples.why: Formal Vy-form breaks the page's informal ty-register convention (e.g. 'najdeš', 'tvého obvodu', 'Všimni si').

editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural and keeps the informal "ty" throughout. The pass threshold ("zodpovědět správně alespoň 16 z nich"), the lock after two failed attempts ("na dva pokusy, zkouška se dočasně zablokuje") and the Credly data-sharing notice all match the English exactly.

The rewritten entry 3 video title is faithful and natural: "jak se problém mapuje na kvantový počítač" and "qubit může představovat uzel v grafu, krok páteře bílkoviny podél diskretizované mřížky a další" keep every example and the "may represent" hedge.

Entry 29 keeps the full caveat chain intact: "odpovídají ketům (sloupcovým vektorům)", "NumPy ... u 1D polí vnitřně nerozlišuje mezi řádkovými a sloupcovými vektory", and "transpozice žádný numerický vliv", ending on "lépe odpovídá ... v Diracově notaci", so nothing drifts and it uses informal "Všimni si".

None of the 9 rewritten entries would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still change four things. In entry 38, "dekvantována" clashes with "dekvantizováno/dekvantizovat" used elsewhere on the page (entries 32, 35), and "se obecně věří hypotéze, že" is an awkward rendering of "widely-believed conjecture". Entry 74 translates the heading as "Vzory Qiskit", while entries 56 and 73 keep "Qiskit patterns" in English. Entry 8 renders "subspace quantum diagonalization" as "diagonalizace kvantového podprostoru" ("diagonalization of the quantum subspace"), which moves "quantum" onto the subspace; entries 43, 48, 61, 71 and 81 are fine.

examples.source: classical hardness (unlikely to be dequantized)
examples.translation: klasickou obtížnost (je nepravděpodobné, že by byla dekvantována)
examples.suggested: klasickou obtížnost (je nepravděpodobné, že by úloha byla dekvantizována)
examples.why: Entries 32 and 35 use dekvantizace/dekvantizovat; 'dekvantována' is a second form of the same term. The feminine ending also makes 'obtížnost' the thing being dequantized, not the problem.

examples.source: it is a widely-believed conjecture that no classical algorithm can compute
examples.translation: se obecně věří hypotéze, že žádný klasický algoritmus nedokáže spočítat
examples.suggested: je obecně přijímanou hypotézou, že žádný klasický algoritmus nedokáže spočítat
examples.why: 'věřit hypotéze' is a calque that reads awkwardly in Czech mathematical prose.

examples.source: Qiskit patterns:
examples.translation: Vzory Qiskit:
examples.suggested: Qiskit patterns:
examples.why: Entries 56 and 73 keep the framework name 'Qiskit patterns' in English. Translating it only in the heading makes the page inconsistent.

examples.source: an overview of subspace quantum diagonalization
examples.translation: přehled diagonalizace kvantového podprostoru
examples.suggested: přehled kvantové diagonalizace v podprostoru
examples.why: This moves 'quantum' onto the subspace. The method is a quantum diagonalization carried out in a subspace, not a diagonalization of a 'quantum subspace'.

editor_note: The heading in [1], "Pokračuj ve svém vzdělávacím cestování", is a stiff calque. "Cestování" means the act of travelling, which is not the metaphorical "journey" the English means. It also doesn't match [0], which correctly uses "vzdělávacích cest". A Czech editor would write "Pokračuj na své vzdělávací cestě". Entries [0] and [2] are faithful and natural, and the informal "ty" register is kept.

examples.source: Continue your learning journey
examples.translation: Pokračuj ve svém vzdělávacím cestování
examples.suggested: Pokračuj na své vzdělávací cestě
examples.why: "Cestování" (travelling) is an unidiomatic word-for-word rendering of "journey". The natural metaphor is "cesta", which [0] already uses.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 8 "Přibližná doba QPU potřebná ke spuštění tohoto experimentu je 10 sekund" matches the English: the quantity (10 seconds), the approximation qualifier and the QPU-time meaning are all kept.

None of the six rewritten entries (91-96) would mislead a learner. The VQD caveat is intact: variational energy cannot fall below the true ground state, orthogonality is only imposed against an approximate ground state, and "Žádná penalizace za překryv tě neudrží mimo skutečný základní stav" matches the English. The problems are small. In entry 96, "uložením nižší tolerance" is stiff, and there is a non-Czech comma before "a případně". In entry 92, "mezi každou aktualizací parametrů" is a calque. In entry 95, "quite close" became the slightly stronger "velmi blízké".

examples.source: imposing lower tolerance for the classical optimizer, and possibly also trying a different ansatz
examples.translation: uložením nižší tolerance pro klasický optimalizátor, a případně také vyzkoušením jiného ansatzu
examples.suggested: nastavením nižší tolerance klasického optimalizátoru a případně také vyzkoušením jiného ansatzu
examples.why: 'Uložit toleranci' is a stiff calque of 'impose'. Czech technical usage is 'nastavit toleranci', and Czech does not put a comma before 'a' in a simple list like this one.

examples.source: and not between every parameter update
examples.translation: a ne mezi každou aktualizací parametrů
examples.suggested: a ne po každé aktualizaci parametrů
examples.why: 'Mezi každou aktualizací' copies the English word for word and sounds odd in Czech. 'Po každé aktualizaci' or 'mezi jednotlivými aktualizacemi' is more natural.

examples.source: our energy estimates for the excited states were actually quite close to the ground state energy
examples.translation: byly ve skutečnosti velmi blízké energii základního stavu
examples.suggested: byly ve skutečnosti dost blízké energii základního stavu
examples.why: 'Velmi' makes 'quite close' slightly stronger. This does not mislead, but 'dost' or 'poměrně' is closer to the English.
